text:
kevin: noticing a spike in NCCL allreduce retries on pcluster-eu2 tonight, jobs hitting timeouts and GPU utilization dropping to 10%
maya: any error lines from the worker logs?
kevin: seeing repeated `IBV_EVENT_QP_FATAL` and `ibv_create_qp: -5` plus long tail in allreduce (p99 up from 12ms to 450ms)
ben: that usually smells like east-west packet drops or MTU/fragmentation on RoCEv2 path
alia: can you paste ethtool -S on mlx5? also tcpdump on udp port 4791 to confirm RoCEv2 retransmits
kevin: attaching quick snippets:
```
# ibstat on one affected node
CA 'mlx5_0' ndev 'eth0'  port 1 -> ACTIVE
link_layer: ETH
sm_lid: 0
port guid: 0x...
```
```
# dmesg excerpt
mlx5_core: port 1 CQE errors increasing: qp 32768: status=0x12 vendor_err=0x0
ibv_event: QP fatal on qp 32768
```
```
# ethtool -S eth0 | grep drop
rx_missed_errors: 0
rx_queue_4_drop: 312
tx_queue_4_drop: 0
```
maya: rx_queue_4_drop creeping up is interesting. Are we seeing ECMP path changes during the MPI window?
ben: also check if any tc or qos shaping was recently pushed on the ToR — small policing bursts can cause UDP micro-dropping and break RoCE reliability
kevin: infra says there was a config roll to enable qos-profile-eu2 yesterday for tenant isolation (low priority classes)
alia: that might be it. RoCEv2 is UDP; any policer on UDP/4791 will drop incast during allreduce. Ask infra to exempt RDMA flows or move to DSCP mapping expected by ToR
kevin: I ran `tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 4791` during a job, saw a high rate of dup/icmp fragmentation-needed responses sporadically
ben: fragmentation-needed points to MTU mismatch somewhere — are we using jumbo (9000) across the whole path?
kevin: nodes are 9000, but the ToR uplinks were recently set to 1500 on a subset for a test VLAN — that could cause fragmentation fallback
maya: two simultaneous issues: (1) policer dropping bursts (2) MTU mismatch causing fragmentation/ICMP and extra latency. Both will break latency-sensitive RDMA traffic
alia: quick mitigation: (A) disable QoS policing for UDP/4791 and DSCP used by RDMA on the ToR for the affected PODs, (B) set path MTU to 1500 on hosts as temporary consistent setting until ToR fixed, or (C) enable UDP segmentation offload adjustments. Which is fastest?
infra-bot: raised ticket INFRA-5239 to rollback qos-profile-eu2 to previous state for 2 racks — ETA 30m
kevin: rolling the MTU to 1500 on the compute nodes now for affected racks to stop fragmentation while infra fixes QoS
ben: also recommend turning off GRO/LRO on eth0 for a reproducible baseline: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off` — that has helped for RoCEv2 debug in the past
kevin: done. re-ran the workload, p99 is down to ~18ms and no QP fatal in last 10m
maya: can we capture ethtool -S and mlx5 counters before/after so we have numbers for postmortem?
kevin: saving outputs and job traces to /var/log/rdma-debug/pcluster-eu2/2099998887.log.tar.gz
alia: long-term fixes: (1) add an explicit RDMA DSCP mapping on ToRs and exempt from per-tenant policing, (2) enforce MTU consistency via config validation in our provisioning, (3) add an infra test that runs a short allreduce on new QoS changes
ben: +1. also consider configuring kernel QP timeout params (rdma_cm_reestablish) as a safety, but that only masks drops — better to fix network
kevin: schedule: infra rolling back qos change now; i'll run a fullerset overnight to validate. If infra can't rollback, i'll migrate jobs to other regions temporarily
maya: do we want an incident page for customer-facing teams? this caused a few internal jobs to fail but no external SLA hit yet
alia: create a short incident note in #incidents summarizing root cause hypothesis (QoS policer + MTU mismatch), mitigations and follow-ups
kevin: thanks all. will update when infra confirms rollback or we see reoccurrence
opsbot: deploy-bot: rollback job for qos-profile-eu2 started (ticket INFRA-5239)
kevin: final note — add a provisioning validation step: deny QoS changes that apply policing to UDP ports used by RDMA unless explicitly approved by eng-runtime
ben: agreed. also add a small probe (single-packet UDP test + PMTU check + DSCP check) as a healthcheck for each rack during provisioning
alia: tagging followups for next week: infra owner (maya), runtime owner (ben), oncall (kevin)
kevin: closing thread, will reopen if anything else pops up
